text: While moving through a rising lock on a river, a privately hired boat contacted the bottom of a bridge and partially flooded. The boat encountered the underside of a swing-bridge that required raising before the lock could fill due to its position outside the specified navigation area. Neighboring individuals provided assistance, which resulted in the vessel being restored to operational status. It is noted that the lock involved was beyond the authorized boundaries designated for use, possibly leading to an oversight by the hire party regarding the specific location or signs related to the swing-bridge.
label: Contact

text: The inland passenger ship contacted a jetty due to being lifted by a wave while berthing, causing no substantial damage. The rubbing strake touched the jetty, but the vessel remained stationary as it sat on the jetty following the wave's lift. After regaining its equilibrium, the vessel released its hold and the rub rail sustained minor damage, affecting a specific area of the running gear and forward mooring equipment. The occupants were unaware that such an occurrence had transpired.
label: Contact

text: The Ro-Ro cargo vessel collided with the breakwater causing damage to the main deck's frame approximately one hundred fifty meters from the intended departure point. The ship veered towards the south due to a navigational error; it had just entered the port when an unexpected wave affected its course. In order to correct the drift, the captain turned sharply to the right to maintain centering within the harbor channel but failed to respond promptly to steering controls. As a result of this delayed maneuver, the ship hit the northern shore of the breakwater forcefully. This resulted in scratches on the port side of the vessel along the frame 138 on the main deck, situated about four meters above sea level, accompanied by slight dents. There were no structural damages visible through initial examinations, although further investigations might uncover more extensive damage.
label: Contact

text: A SAR vessel was conducting a return to port for recovery operations when it encountered an accident during the stern lifting maneuver. The starboard horn's bend occurred due to excessive loading, causing the starboard propeller blade to break off. Upon engaging astern propulsion and propelling forward while still in the carriage, this action led to severe deformation of the starboard side of the vessel. No casualties or additional damages were recorded.
label: Contact

text: A Marine Autonomous Surface Ship encountered an Offshore Substation while conducting a survey. Upon loss of Visual Satellite Terminal communications due to a blind spot within the satellite coverage area, the ship continued for about 50 meters before coming to a halt, roughly 50 meters northwest of the substation. Secondary communication systems were initiated, though their reception was of low quality. Tertiary communication attempts were unsuccessful. During this period, the vessel's control mechanisms were rendered unusable for around eight minutes, preventing any further actions by the crew. Initially, there was no response to the vessel's movements or its condition. However, after four minutes, a secondary signal allowed communication to be restored, and the ship was directed away from the substation.
label: Contact

text: The pleasure yacht encountered an issue with its sailing equipment, causing the propeller to fail. As a result, the auxiliary engine could not be started, and the vessel ended up being trapped on a dolphin at a nearby LNG jetty due to wind force. Initially, a tugboat attempted to pull the yacht away from the jetty but abandoned it after drifting in the channel. The local lifeboat service deployed a search and rescue vessel that eventually retrieved the sailing yacht and transported it safely to port without any injuries, pollution, or damage.
label: Contact

text: The vessel was entering a lock when its stern collided with a part of the lock structure. At that time, there was a strong gust of wind catching the stern, leading to an accident involving the vessel. As a result, the hull received damage to two fenders, each of which was removed due to their position relative to the railing. Upon arriving on the other side, some paint marks were noted on the deck but further structural damage was not observed. Additionally, inspections of the fuel tanks revealed that no water ingress occurred.
label: Contact

text: The SAR vessel became entangled with an unidentified underwater obstruction, leading to damage to its propeller blades. The anchor was obstructed while navigating near this submerged entity. During attempts to release the anchor using a lifeboat, the vessel's starboard propeller encountered and struck a portion beneath the water's surface. This collision resulted in severe damage to the propeller blades. Consequently, the anchor was eventually released, allowing the lifeboat to resume its training exercises safely.
label: Contact

text: A coastal passenger ship collided with a vehicular bridge during its approach to a dock. Under the prevailing tidal and meteorological conditions, it was impossible for the vessel to execute the maneuver required to avoid the bridge. As a result, the stern of the ship struck the bridge, causing an emergency stop. Passengers sustained minor injuries requiring on-site medical attention. No structural damage was reported inside the passenger cabins.
label: Contact

text: A cargo vessel collided with the quay wall while attempting to dock at its berth. The collision was caused by a wave causing the vessel to be pushed onto the quay.
label: Contact

text: The guard vessel collided with a navigational buoy. This collision led to a damaged hull and water entry into the machinery space. Search and rescue services arrived and extracted the water from this area, enabling the vessel to return to port on its own propulsion system for necessary repairs. There were no reports of injuries among the crew.
label: Contact

text: During an SAR operation on return to port, a vessel collided with its carriage while being retrieved from water. This collision caused the propeller to bend. There were no reported injuries among personnel but the propeller sustained damage as a result.
label: Contact

text: A yacht struck a bridge, causing a fractured injury to one crew member. The accident also resulted in two fatalities; fortunately, only one crew member suffered harm. Upon arrival at the scene, they were taken by ambulance for further medical treatment. Toxicology tests revealed that all individuals involved had been under the influence of alcohol.
label: Contact

text: The vessel collided with the outer lock gate while docking at Port A due to improper handling or a malfunctioning mechanism causing the collision. There were no damages reported on the vessel.
label: Contact

text: A general cargo vessel collided with dockside equipment inside a tidal lock while navigating through one under turbulent weather conditions characterized by strong gusts and choppy sea. No incidents such as injuries, pollution, or structural damage occurred following the collision. The encounter took place when the vessel was passing through the lock amidst high winds and waves. As a result of the stormy conditions, the vessel managed to come into close proximity to the locked door's exterior, causing its stern to rest along the dockside structure. Despite this unusual alignment between the ship and the dock, there were no significant physical harm inflicted upon either the lock or the vessel itself.
label: Contact

text: The general cargo vessel collided with a bollard while moving alongside the berth. As it was underway, its port quarter struck the quay's edge and impacted the bollard. Although there was damage to the bollard itself, no visible harm or structural impact occurred on the vessel.
label: Contact

text: The wind turbine crew boat encountered an unidentified entity. The vessel remained on its port side while the captain experienced a bank effect followed by contact with it.
label: Contact

text: An SAR vessel struck a rock reef while performing duties for a burning ship incident. Acting as a barrier, the condition of the sea led the vessel into proximity with the rocky area. Upon touching, the propeller incurred burring damage which necessitated subsequent filing.
label: Contact

text: The ro-ro passenger ship collided with a buoying dock structure while attempting to dock, leading to structural damage on its stern. During this maneuver, the ship's portside stern touched the outer edge of a buoyant piling, causing the walkway connecting the buoying structure and the principal steering ramp to shift position abnormally. The incident resulted in minor hull injuries due to a metal component of the buoying structure being knocked off. There were no casualties reported in the accident.
label: Contact

text: During a night navigation exercise within a harbor, a sailing training ship had an encounter with a navigation landmark. After departing the harbor under nighttime conditions for the purpose of exercising navigational skills, the vessel came into contact with said mark. Although no severe structural damages were observed, there was slight damage to the boat's exterior appearance.
label: Contact

text: A general cargo ship encountered the quay while en route to the harbor. No injuries were reported among the crew, nor was there any environmental contamination. The vessel suffered a minor indentation on its bow flare due to the collision. This incident has been communicated to both the vessel's class and the Swedish Accident Investigation Agency along with the Port State Control (PSC) inspectors.
label: Contact

text: During the maneuvering operation of a general cargo vessel, there was contact with a berth. An operator's task involved steering a general cargo vessel towards a berth while another person aboard served as a pilot. While making its way to the berth, the ship collided with the pier, causing light damages to its bow section and affecting the pier itself. As the vessel approached the dockside, strong tidal currents caused the stern area of the vessel to catch up to the land, leading to an accelerated movement. Despite the efforts by both the crew and the pilot to regain control, the vessel's bow managed to strike the pier. The pilot had earlier informed the team that they were responsible for guiding the vessel but after reaching the dock, the captain requested to direct the navigation process instead. It seems possible the captain might have overestimated his skills in operating the vessel and underestimated the impact of the current and tide conditions.
label: Contact

text: A fire broke out in the galley of an offshore support vessel. The blaze was quickly contained and no structural damage or injuries were reported on board. There was no need for external assistance from coastguards.
label: Fire / Explosion

text: A dredger experienced an electrical fire in its laundry room due to flooding caused by the overflow from the greywater tank. The fire resulted from a faulty non-return valve (NRV) that allowed contaminated water to return into the vessel's greywater system. The faulty pump operation also contributed to the situation. Fortunately, no personnel were harmed, and the blaze was promptly brought under control by the on-board team.
label: Fire / Explosion

text: A cargo ship suffered a fire in its hold as it was being loaded with scrap metal. Initially, an alert was triggered by a fire inside one of the ship's holds, which housed such materials. The crew responded promptly by attempting to control the blaze and contacted local authorities for assistance. Fire crews arrived on site to deal with the situation, effectively putting out the flames. There were no reported injuries among the crew members, nor any environmental impact from this maritime incident.
label: Fire / Explosion

text: The tug encountered a fire aboard its starboard engine during operation. Fire alarms triggered in the engine room as the tug pushed alongside another vessel. Crew members were alerted and promptly arrived at the scene. A fire was detected on the portside engine. Immediate emergency shutdown procedures were executed due to the imminent danger. Upon closer inspection, evidence suggested that the fuel line, designed for efficient fuel delivery, had become misaligned and was rubbing against the edge of the engine cover, leading to friction and potential heat build-up. This friction eventually caused a leak in the fuel line, allowing fuel to come into contact with exposed metal surfaces, igniting the flammable mixture. Subsequently, when the flames intensified, they led to melting of the fuel hose, which also compromised the integrity of the pressure gauge located near the inlet manifold. This action further exacerbated the fire's spread by allowing compressed air to blow more vigorously, enhancing the fire's intensity.
label: Fire / Explosion

text: A general cargo ship encountered a fire within its cargo hold because of dampened grain. As the ship was being loaded with grain, the crew observed that some parts of the cargo had started to smoke. Upon arrival of the local fire brigade, it was confirmed that the fire had been put out but toxic gases had been released from the burning grains. The ship's captain then ordered the discharge of all remaining grain and proceeded to detain the vessel at the port. Unfortunately, despite this precautionary measure, an unfortunate event occurred; no one on board sustained any injury. Additionally, minimal physical damage was noted on the vessel, though concerns were raised about potential environmental contamination.
label: Fire / Explosion

text: A small fire occurred aboard a dredging vessel, causing minor damage to the pump drive transformer. The fire was detected within the pump drive room, where a small flame originating from electrical cabling within the transformer housing was quickly extinguished using CO2 extinguishers.
label: Fire / Explosion

text: The hired yacht experienced an onboard fire that required crew relocation to another vessel. A nearby moored motor cruiser also had its engine room affected by smoke, prompting an evacuation. Emergency services discovered that the engine room was excessively warm but could not locate any fire. Fortunately, all passengers remained unharmed.
label: Fire / Explosion

text: A Ro-Ro passenger vessel experienced a fire in the engine room shortly after departing the harbor. The blaze was promptly extinguished using an onboard firefighting equipment. Initial investigations revealed that the fire resulted from a loose connection point on the lubricating oil sensor piping, which subsequently spilled oil onto the overheated machinery.
label: Fire / Explosion

text: The vessel suffered from an electrical malfunction that ignited. No injuries or substantial damage resulted. The overcurrent protection device malfunctioned, necessitating its replacement.
label: Fire / Explosion

text: A fire broke out on board a Ro-Ro passenger vessel, causing significant damage. The fire was triggered by issues with the aft generator's alternator. Upon noticing smoke, the crew used a CO2 extinguisher to control the blaze. However, the fire subsequently rekindled, necessitating the use of a foam extinguisher. Despite efforts to replace the generators, further damage including the alternator and potentially its wiring resulted from the flames.
label: Fire / Explosion

text: A failure in the alternator bearing occurred aboard an inland ro-pax ship while it was moored. Smoke emanated from the engine room's ventilation systems upon activation of the fire alarm system. Three crew members immediately began firefighting efforts and contacted shore-based emergency services. They successfully contained the blaze, which was centered around the aft main engine's alternator, before external firefighters arrived. It is stated that the engine room should remain closed to prevent potential reignition risks. The ignition point was attributed to a malfunctioning bearing on the aft engine alternator. No injuries nor environmental contamination were reported.
label: Fire / Explosion

text: During towing operations, an inland waterways vessel experienced a sinking event. The vessel encountered flooding issues while being towed. This led to its unfortunate demise. Before departing, no damages were observed on board. A total of 120 liters of diesel fuel were present aboard; however, there was no evidence of leakage. Immediate salvage measures have been initiated for the affected vessel.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A motor cruiser faced water infiltration that necessitated towing to the port. The vessel had to be rescued using a specialized boat for assistance in getting it back to port. After being pulled out from the water, efforts were made to secure the vessel again to avoid additional water intrusion issues.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A pilot vessel experienced water ingress and was subsequently towed by a lifeboat due to this incident. It suffered from hull damage leading to water entry, resulting in beaching at the harbor entrance under the supervision of lifeboat personnel who brought pump units aboard for assistance. Comprehensive inspections were carried out across all vessel compartments; these revealed them to be undamaged. Subsequently, the vessel was towed back into port using a lifeboat. The identified degree of damage amounted to a breach measuring approximately 70 cm by 10 cm.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A boat carrying three individuals sank rapidly due to water ingress, resulting in all occupants being submerged wearing life jackets. The victims were successfully recovered by rescue teams using a lifeboat and assistance from nearby boats. Due to quick response times, no further air support was required. The survivors were handed over to emergency medical personnel for care.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A stern trawler began taking in water and sounded an emergency signal through a VHF radio channel. Two commercial vessels, two local lifeboat crews, and a rescue helicopter responded. A lifeboat crew used their pumps to help stabilize the situation, preventing additional water from entering. Meanwhile, the helicopter's winch operator managed to bring in a pump for the distressed vessel. All operations were successful, and the trawler made it back to port under the convoy of lifeboats without any major injuries or significant structural damage.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: The yacht began to take on water, necessitating a tow. An emergency position indicating radio beacon (EPIRB) signal was received. A sailboat experienced flooding. Immediate coordination was established with the closest rescue service to transport the boat safely back to shore. There were no reported injuries.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A fishing vessel encountered a water ingress issue that necessitated towing it to safety using a lifeboat. The stern trawler experienced flooding due to this situation. Two rescue vessels were dispatched to manage the inflow, utilizing both their pumps and methods to staunch the leak. One of these lifeboats successfully evacuated the distressed vessel's crew to a dockside location before leaving them secure at a moored buoy. Unfortunately, no human casualties occurred during the incident.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: While engaged in dredging operations in shallow waters adjacent to another fishing vessel, a fishing craft experienced an accident. The operator successfully deployed the dredge line and bags and began towing operations. As tension on the dredge line increased, the vessel's bow turned sharply towards the starboard side. Realizing this situation, the skipper took necessary actions to prevent further loss of control. However, due to the limited depth of the surrounding waters, the vessel rapidly capsized. Despite being equipped with a lifejacket, the captain managed to reach safety by climbing onto the port side. The other fishing vessel promptly rescued the injured captain.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A fishing boat began filling up with water and asked for help. Upon finding a leak, it started taking in water. Initially, the pumps managed to cope, but assistance from rescue teams was called due to the water level rising. Despite this, the boat made it back to the harbor by itself.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: The wooden crabber experienced flooding that led to its sinking. Two individuals aboard the vessel were successfully saved from the water using their life rafts. Reports indicate that wreckage was found in the area after the sinking occurred.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A harbor tug encountered a yacht while passing it at high speed, resulting in significant splashing that entered the yacht via a hatches. No damage or injuries were reported.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: In heavy weather, a yacht developed issues with its port hull window causing it to begin taking on water. Crew members initially tried to alert authorities via VHF radio without success. After contacting emergency services through their mobile phones, the coastguard sent out a lifeboat to assist. However, due to a shortage of available life jackets (seven) and man liferafts (four), they decided to prioritize evacuation. Thankfully, all individuals aboard were successfully rescued, and the vessel was subsequently towed back to port.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A recreational boat began taking in water due to a breach at the hull. A non-commercial fishing vessel experienced this issue, which resulted from a damaged wooden plank. Local rescue personnel were able to assist the vessel using a lifeboat, facilitating its return to port for drainage operations. Once at the dock, the vessel completed these efforts without any injuries or environmental concerns.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: During a routine hull cleaning operation on a cruise ship, sea water accidentally entered a ballast tank intended for inspection. The ballast tank, which had been emptied beforehand, ruptured due to inadequate sealing around the entry point. A professional team immediately addressed the issue by installing a temporary sealant plug to prevent further intrusion and ensure the safety of all passengers onboard. No pollutants were released into the environment, nor did it compromise the overall stability of the vessel.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: The non-commercial wooden fishing vessel encountered difficulties due to loss of propulsion and began taking on water. Although additional pumps were deployed, the vessel still sank, resulting in the successful rescue and transfer of both crew members to shore. Efforts were made using lifeboats and a helicopter for assistance in recovering them. No injuries or damages occurred among the crew.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A narrowboat began to experience flooding in its engine room due to an issue with its plumbing system. As a consequence, the engine failed, causing the boat to lose power. Emergency personnel responded by dispatching another vessel equipped with pumps to extract the water from the engine room. The damaged narrowboat was then towed to a nearby pier for repair work. No individuals were injured during this event, nor did it lead to any form of environmental contamination.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A fishing vessel experienced water intrusion, requesting aid. Upon detecting a breach, three personnel aboard proceeded to evacuate to a life raft, while donning life jackets. A Distress Alert via DSC was initiated, followed by an aerial evacuation of the distressed crew. The fishing vessel's immediate vicinity was assessed for further risks. SAR vessels and helicopters responded to the situation. The vessel was subsequently towed to a nearby harbor for maintenance and repairs.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: The ship struck the dock while sailing in a wide river, causing severe damage to its hull. The passengers attempted to turn the vessel around near the waterfront, but the stern port side corner encountered a metal dock wall, resulting in structural cracks. Despite their efforts to remain afloat, the boat began taking on water. Consequently, they managed to pull the ship onto the shore where they removed numerous objects before eventually sinking due to lack of buoyancy. While no environmental impact resulted from the incident, debris like cushions floated away after cleanup operations concluded.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A vessel experienced flooding due to seasickness, necessitating it be towed by a lifeboat to the harbor. With just two individuals aboard, the vessel suffered from an accidental influx of seawater prompting assistance. A lifeboat arrived and promptly aided in the retrieval process, ensuring safe return to the port. No injuries or damages were observed following this event. Both passengers adhered to maritime safety regulations by being properly equipped with life jackets.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A fishing vessel experienced water entering a ballast tank due to a damaged ballast tank valve. This caused sea water to seep back into the tank during operations as a guardship for an oil rig. As a result, the vessel required repairs.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: The ro-pax vessel suffered water infiltration into two of its forward compartments during docking at the initial destination port. Upon receiving an alarm from the bilges indicating a presence of seawater in these areas, it became apparent that the anchor's securement had been improperly executed, leading to punctures in the ship's hull. As a result, water entered through these openings. This issue did not lead to any form of pollution nor caused harm to personnel aboard.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A fishing vessel began taking in water, necessitating a tow. One of the crew noticed that the engine room bilge alarm sounded because there was water seeping through the deck plates. To address this issue, the crew deployed two submersible pumps in the engine room bilge and started the main engine room pump. They also prepared two lifeboats and ensured all crew members wore life jackets. Unfortunately, there were no injuries among the crew. The source of the flooding stemmed from aged piping, but the team successfully contained the situation and asked for assistance.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A fishing vessel experienced water ingress and subsequently sank while carrying two crew members. The crew fled in a life raft when the situation worsened. SAR teams responded immediately to provide assistance. Unfortunately, the vessel sank despite efforts to save it. Both crew members survived but needed immediate medical attention upon arrival on shore.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A recreational cabin cruiser capsized near a bustling beach as it approached within dangerously close proximity to shore. Five people aboard perished when the vessel succumbed to its submerged condition and subsequently plunged into the ocean. These individuals managed to escape before being overwhelmed by the water, which led them to be retrieved from the sea. Post-rescue, these victims received medical attention at local facilities, including paramedic assistance. The injured were hospitalized but released after displaying minimal symptoms.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A fishing vessel experienced flooding which necessitated towing it back to port for repairs.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A motor yacht experienced flooding. The crew managed to contain the leak and safely transferred the distressed vessel into the harbor. A specialized rescue boat was dispatched to help an auxiliary craft that had taken on water. Due to issues at the cooling water intake, the rescue boat's crew halted the entry point and guided the distressed craft back onto its home waters using its own power.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A yacht began flooding, necessitating a rescue by lifeboats for its return to the port. Crew members were perplexed about the source of the water ingress.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A ship encountered flooding due to a breach in its seawater cooling system. It was conducting an assistance mission when a warning signal indicated an overflow in the engine compartment's bilges. A member of the crew responded to inspect the situation; they discovered considerable amounts of seawater within the engine room through the bilge pump alarm activation. Upon examining the problem area, it became evident that there was a leak originating from the connection point between the main seawater line and the cooling system. This location featured insufficient overlap at the joint where a flexible hose transitioned onto the larger pipe. During the inspection, two jubilee clips securing this segment appeared to be loose. To resolve the issue, the flexible hose was carefully moved upward to reconnect the connections securely, after which both jubilee clips were tightened accordingly. After successfully pumping out the excess water, the ship resumed operations.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A sailing yacht ran aground on a sandbank, causing a keel to break off and subsequently capsizing with two crew members aboard. Search and rescue personnel launched their vessels upon arrival at the scene to recover the distressed crew from the water. No further medical assistance was necessary. The sunken vessel was noted to have its mast visible above the surface; however, there is uncertainty regarding the presence of any remaining fuel or risks associated with leakage. Efforts are underway to mark the wreck site with a buoys to ensure safe navigation through the area while awaiting possible salvage operations.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: During an exercise, a SAR vessel experienced flooding due to a damaged hose connecting it to the bilge system. The affected vessel was able to safely return to port using its engines and confirmed that the leak originated from a malfunctioning engine coolant line. No injuries, environmental contamination, or structural damage were reported in this instance.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: The recreational motor vessel encountered issues with its propeller shaft, leading to water entering the hull. Initially, the bilge pumps managed to handle the situation; however, SAR assistance was required to safely maneuver the vessel.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: The sailing yacht collided with a rock while anchored and experienced water entry. Three crew members were aboard, requiring assistance to remove seawater from the ship. A SAR vessel arrived equipped with a salvaging pump, deploying personnel for assessment and towing the vessel to a safer location should further intervention be necessary.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A fishing vessel faced flooding due to a broken water pump casing. This issue led to saltwater flowing into the engine room through a service pump. The faulty pump was capable of directing water both to the deck wash pipe and creating suction within the bilge system.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: During a sailing competition, a yacht took on water while racing downwind towards its destination. As it sailed into a turn, the vessel began filling with water due to a broken hatch cover. Eventually, the yacht capsized and three crew members managed to escape to the surface. A nearby rescue boat picked up one survivor, but another boat had technical issues and could not reach them, leaving the remaining two aboard their sinking yacht until they also drowned. Despite no reported injuries among the crew or any accidents during their voyage, all parties wore life jackets.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A pleasure vessel experienced a flooding situation requiring assistance. The crew was safely recovered by the Eastbourne and Newhaven RNLI ALB's and CG R136.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: While alongside another vessel, a pleasure craft experienced flooding from a leak that resulted in its sinking. Inside a motor vessel, which was anchored beside another, a single crew member was initially trapped when it started to flood as it was moored. They made their way to the wheelhouse roof after managing to escape. Although affected by hypothermia from the cold nighttime air and the cold water, the crew member sustained minor injuries. Despite this, the boat was determined to be a total loss. The leaked area might have been caused by hull damage or a failed seacock valve.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A fishing boat was swept away by a surge and subsequently capsized, resulting in the loss of life for three personnel onboard.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A sailing vessel began taking on water, leading to the assistance of a search and rescue vessel. Subsequently, the same event necessitated the intervention of the Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI) for recovery purposes. The sailing vessel experienced an influx of water, resulting in one person overboarded. The boat received assistance from the RNLI crew who managed to secure it before transporting it safely to a designated marina.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A service vessel encountered flooding caused by uncorrected water entry through its seawater system. Crew failure resulted in insufficient isolation measures during maintenance activities for seawater strainers. This led to approximately 50-60 cubic meters of seawater entering the engine room. A bilge alarm was triggered upon detection. Attempted repairs failed; one crew member managed to isolate a valve, while another successfully replaced the strainer cover. Shore-based assistance was called for to drain the accumulated water.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A fishing vessel encountered a minor breach in its hull causing it to take on some water. Utilizing the onboard manual bilge pump, they managed to control the water entry effectively. The vessel proceeded on its own until reaching port where assistance from a search and rescue (SAR) vessel became necessary. The SAR vessel then provided additional support through the use of another bilge pump.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A fishing boat experienced water entry due to a hole. Upon arrival at the scene, a rescue craft equipped with a pump intervened to save the vessel and bring it safely back to port.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A speedboat experienced partial submersion near a riverbank where all personnel survived an encounter unharmed. The boat was salvaged by its owner without any injuries reported and the situation was resolved through appropriate measures.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A fishing boat encountered water intrusion while deploying fishing nets. Crew members observed water flowing into the vessel through the port side. They resolved this issue by activating on-board pumps. Despite minor flooding, the boat safely returned to shore using only one functioning engine.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A historic sail training vessel began to take on water. Crew members immediately initiated an emergency call for help. In response, a nearby search and rescue craft arrived to facilitate the evacuation and pumping of the water from the ship. The sail training vessel successfully reached port and proceeded to a dry dock for repairs aimed at addressing the leaking issue. Throughout this event, there were no incidents resulting in any injuries or environmental contamination.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A fishing vessel experienced a broken pipe that caused flooding of its engine room. The crew isolated the valve before the engine was submerged into water. Unfortunately, when the water reached the generators, the vessel stopped functioning. As a result, the generators sustained damage due to water ingress through their fans.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A sailing vessel took in water and was rescued by maritime rescue assets. The vessel was calling for help due to experiencing flooding. Various ships, such as advanced lifeboats (ALBs), were dispatched to provide assistance because their onboard systems could not handle the influx of water. Crew members from the ALBs were deployed to assist in pumping out the water and lowering four crew members onto shore while they were met by the coast guard team. The vessel was subsequently taken into the marina accompanied by the captain aboard. All individuals involved were unharmed.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A fishing vessel suffered a crack in its stern corner weld due to water seeping into the aft fuel tank, causing the main engine to fail. The vessel's trawl door also cracked, leading to seawater entry and disabling the engine. Fuel pumps and injectors were compromised, preventing the ship from moving forward. The vessel could potentially lose 2 tonnes of diesel. It was towed by another fishing vessel, which safely docked at harbor. During towing, the vessel listeed slightly to the starboard side to reduce the risk of additional pollution. The aft port fuel tank was pumped, and repair work is ongoing. No one was injured.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: The fishing vessel experienced flooding that led to no injuries or additional damage. Despite this initial issue, the vessel was safely guided into the harbor by an assisting fishing boat. The vessel had two automatic pumps and five crew members onboard. No other accidents or damages occurred during this event.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A recreational boat experienced water intrusion followed by flooding. In about 200 meters of water, the vessel sank. Nearby assistance arrived and saved the lone crew member; however, the boat's occupants were protected from entering the water.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: An excursion craft foundered close to a harbor's entrance. No harm was sustained, and the craft was retrieved when tides allowed. Having two crew aboard, one of them wearing a life jacket, the craft operated using both its primary and secondary outboards positioned at the rear. Approaching the eastern seawall, a fishing line snarled around the outboard propeller. Attempting to disentangle it, the team moved aft to assist. This maneuver shifted the vessel's center of gravity below the surface, causing water ingress and eventual sinking. The crew was saved by another passing vessel and transported safely ashore without any injuries. A SAR vessel dispatched equipped with a salvage pump arrived to evaluate the situation and potentially tow the vessel safely ashore.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A fishing vessel encountered flooding due to a broken water pump casing. This issue led to contamination from saltwater entering the engine room through the deck washpipe, potentially affecting its operational systems such as the bilge pumps.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A sailing yacht capsized, causing all three persons on board to abandon ship. As a result, the crew had to be rescued and brought ashore. Only minor injuries were suffered by the crew during the rescue operation, necessitating an ambulance's presence. Despite this, there is no evidence of any environmental contamination from the incident. Unfortunately, the cause of the sinking remains undisclosed, as does any physical damage to the wreckage.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A pleasure boat encountered difficulties and began taking on water, necessitating a tow to safety. The vessels involved were provided assistance by Eastbourne RNLI's ALB 140 and Newhaven RNLI's CGR129, alongside R136.
label: Flooding / Foundering

text: A SAR vessel collided with a slipway structure while attempting to recover a lifeboat. The rudder stock came into contact with the slipway, causing it to briefly ground against the structure before the keel settled properly within the keel way. Although there were no reported crew injuries, the rudder stock sustained some damage.
label: Grounding / Stranding

text: A yacht became stranded on a sandbank. The crew initially sent out a MAYDAY signal but later upgraded it to PAN-PAN when their vessel remained anchored. Despite this, there were no immediate threats, damages, environmental impacts, or injuries reported.
label: Grounding / Stranding

text: A chartered sailing vessel collided with a submerged reef and required recovery through the use of a lifeboat. The vessel had experienced a propulsion failure, causing it to run aground on a sandbank. Crew members issued a Mayday signal and deployed an anchor to secure their position until rescue arrived. The damaged vessel was subsequently lifted out of the water for repair. No injuries, damages, or environmental impacts were noted following the event.
label: Grounding / Stranding

text: A fishing vessel encountered difficulty in trying to depart from a harbor due to grounding. It attempted to depart the harbor, but upon unboarding, it got stuck. Despite this setback, the vessel managed to free itself without any reported damage or injuries.
label: Grounding / Stranding

text: An angling vessel experienced an engine failure resulting in its beaching against the rocks. A single individual remained onboard the stricken vessel, which became ensnared against the shoreline. Local search and rescue teams responded to the scene. All individuals aboard were successfully rescued from the distressed vessel, while efforts continued to refloat the damaged craft. Neither significant structural damage nor any injuries occurred during this maritime emergency.
